gaps.term: q avoids all numerators and denominators
gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: This does not follow from the requirement that q not divide the denominator xi: nothing given says q avoids the numerators, nor which 'finitely many matrices' are meant (M, the elimination factors F_1, F_2 and their inverses?) or why a fixed prime q can be chosen to avoid all of them. The reader also needs this to see that F_1, F_2 stay invertible modulo q^b, which the page never says.

gaps.term: why H_sigma <- H_sigma + D_tau needs an interchange but the additions cost O(V)
gaps.quote: So the shear needs $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: The page never says why adding D_tau into H_sigma directly is expensive while adding H_sigma into D_tau (and setting D_tau to H_sigma - D_tau) is cheap. The only cost fact given, the cited O(V) bound, covers linear transformations of H alone or D alone, not additions that mix an H field into a D field, so the reader cannot check that the two additions are O(V) or that the interchange is the costly part.

gaps.quote: The paper shows $N<2L_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}R$.
gaps.note: From s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b, the inequality N < 2L_b gives -N + 2L_b > 0 and hence s_b > W_b R, the opposite of what is claimed; the reader cannot check the conclusion from what the page gives.
